title: Monarch: Legacy of Monsters
synopsis: Your grandfather's basement contains seventeen file cabinets, a key to a Tokyo apartment, and a black-and-white photograph of him with a Titan. You inherit it all. Try to stay alive.

nodes.text: You inherit, alongside a paid-off mortgage and a sad fish, a box of files marked MONARCH — TOP SECRET. Your half-brother you didn't know existed sits across the church. The distance between Half-Brother, Half-Stranger and Page One begins with the choice between “Introduce yourself to him” and “Walk past and read the files first.”

choices.text: Introduce yourself to him
choices.consequence: Family arrives unexpectedly. You introduce yourself to him. The path to Half-Brother, Half-Stranger opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Walk past and read the files first
choices.consequence: You walk past and read the files first. The path to Page One opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Kentaro is your age, raised in Tokyo, equally surprised. He has half the photographs you have. The puzzle, you realize, was always meant to be two-handed. The distance between Tim, the Recruiter and The Apartment in Tokyo begins with the choice between “Compare files together immediately” and “Buy him a drink first.”

choices.text: Compare files together immediately
choices.consequence: Trust before you've earned it. You choose to compare files together immediately. By Tim, the Recruiter, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Buy him a drink first
choices.consequence: You choose to buy him a drink first. By The Apartment in Tokyo, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: The first file is a map with a red circle around an island in the Pacific. The second is a casualty list — civilian, military, both. The third is a photograph of a creature that should not, by current physics, exist.

choices.text: Read every file before you act
choices.consequence: You read every file before you act. The path to Tim, the Recruiter opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Take the most actionable file and move
choices.consequence: You commit to take the most actionable file and move. It carries you toward The Apartment in Tokyo, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: A man in his thirties, polite, badly dressed, finds you at a coffee shop. 'Monarch wants to help,' he says. Choose “Go with Tim to a Monarch safehouse” and Lee Shaw, Old comes into view; choose “Refuse and run with the files” and the road bends toward The Map Pin.

choices.text: Go with Tim to a Monarch safehouse
choices.consequence: You choose to go with Tim to a Monarch safehouse. By Lee Shaw, Old, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Refuse and run with the files
choices.consequence: You commit to refuse and run with the files. It carries you toward The Map Pin, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Inside the apartment is a phone that still works, a kettle, and a wall covered in photographs of the same family — yours, at different decades. Your grandfather kept two lives. The paths divide here: “Photograph the wall for the record” leads into Lee Shaw, Old, while “Sit on the floor and let it hit you” makes The Map Pin the next reckoning.

choices.text: Photograph the wall for the record
choices.consequence: You commit to photograph the wall for the record. It carries you toward Lee Shaw, Old, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Sit on the floor and let it hit you
choices.consequence: You sit on the floor and let it hit you. The path to The Map Pin opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Lee Shaw — your grandfather's old partner, supposedly dead, very alive — walks out of a back room in a leather coat. He looks at you, then Kentaro, then back. Choose “Trust Shaw” and The Outpost comes into view; choose “Verify Shaw first” and the road bends toward The Frequency.

choices.text: Trust Shaw
choices.consequence: You commit to trust Shaw. It carries you toward The Outpost, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Verify Shaw first
choices.consequence: You verify Shaw first. The path to The Frequency opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: On the wall there is a single new pin in a place that wasn't there in any other file — a pin in Kansas. Your grandfather was, somehow, tracking a Titan in Kansas. You don't know why.

choices.text: Go to Kansas
choices.consequence: You choose to go to Kansas. By The Outpost, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Triangulate from Tokyo first
choices.consequence: You commit to triangulate from Tokyo first. It carries you toward The Frequency, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: A small Monarch outpost outside a town that doesn't appear on highway maps. The team here is friendly and scared. They show you a tunnel that goes very, very far down. “Descend with them” draws you toward First Encounter; “Send Kentaro down; stay with the data” leaves The Apex Cinemas waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Descend with them
choices.consequence: You descend with them. The path to First Encounter opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Send Kentaro down; stay with the data
choices.consequence: You send Kentaro down; stay with the data. The path to The Apex Cinemas opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Shaw shows you a recording — Titan calls layered on top of each other. The pattern, he claims, is a language. Your grandfather had translated it partially. The files have the rest. Choose “Translate it together” and First Encounter comes into view; choose “Take the recording to a linguist friend” and the road bends toward The Apex Cinemas.

choices.text: Translate it together
choices.consequence: Tackle the hard problem. You commit to translate it together. It carries you toward First Encounter, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Take the recording to a linguist friend
choices.consequence: You take the recording to a linguist friend. The path to The Apex Cinemas opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Through a Hollow Earth tunnel: a Titan. Real. Large. Calm. It looks at you the way a dog looks at someone it has decided is not a threat. Its eye is the size of a small car.

choices.text: Sit still and let it pass
choices.consequence: You choose to sit still and let it pass. By The Files Online, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Try to record its call
choices.consequence: You choose to try to record its call. By The Hatchling, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Apex Cybernetics has, you discover, infiltrated Monarch's leadership. The company that wants to weaponize Titans is the company that just hired half your grandfather's old friends. The betrayal is, briefly, more painful than the kaiju.

choices.text: Plan to expose Apex
choices.consequence: Counter the corporation. You plan to expose Apex. The path to The Files Online opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Plan to undermine them from inside
choices.consequence: You choose to plan to undermine them from inside. By The Hatchling, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You upload your grandfather's files to a trusted journalist with a 48-hour fuse. If you're not heard from in 48, the files publish. It is the only insurance you have that isn't a Titan. The distance between The Council Vote and Reunion begins with the choice between “Keep moving and rely on the fuse” and “Confront the saboteur in Monarch leadership.”

choices.text: Keep moving and rely on the fuse
choices.consequence: You commit to keep moving and rely on the fuse. It carries you toward The Council Vote, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Confront the saboteur in Monarch leadership
choices.consequence: You choose to confront the saboteur in Monarch leadership. By Reunion, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: In a containment lab you find a small Titan — newborn, blue-eyed, frightened. Apex was going to weaponize it. The hatchling, you realize, has been responding to its mother's calls in the recordings Shaw played. “Release the hatchling to its mother” draws you toward The Council Vote; “Move it to a Monarch sanctuary” leaves Reunion waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Release the hatchling to its mother
choices.consequence: You commit to release the hatchling to its mother. It carries you toward The Council Vote, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Move it to a Monarch sanctuary
choices.consequence: You move it to a Monarch sanctuary. The path to Reunion opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Monarch's old families convene a council vote — keep the files secret, or release them. Your grandfather was the swing vote a generation ago. You are, terrifyingly, the swing vote now. To choose “Vote for release” means meeting The Press Conference; “Vote for limited disclosure” sends you toward The Family Dinner instead.

choices.text: Vote for release
choices.consequence: You choose to vote for release. By The Press Conference, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Vote for limited disclosure
choices.consequence: You vote for limited disclosure. The path to The Family Dinner opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You and Kentaro stand at the mouth of a tunnel and watch the hatchling find its mother. The sound the mother Titan makes shakes the air. It is, somehow, joy. To choose “Stay in the work” means meeting The Press Conference; “Hand the work to others and go home” sends you toward The Family Dinner instead.

choices.text: Stay in the work
choices.consequence: This is your inheritance. You stay in the work. The path to The Press Conference opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Hand the work to others and go home
choices.consequence: You commit to hand the work to others and go home. It carries you toward The Family Dinner, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: A press conference releases redacted but real information about Monarch, Titans, and Apex. The world panics for a week and then, weirdly, adjusts. Humans are good at adjusting to the impossible. They always have been.

choices.text: Take a leadership role in the new public Monarch
choices.consequence: You choose to take a leadership role in the new public Monarch. By Years Later, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Step back to advisor
choices.consequence: You commit to step back to advisor. It carries you toward The Map, Closing, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Kentaro and his mother visit your home. Your own mother, baffled, sets six places. The dinner is — given the day — startlingly ordinary. You realize the inheritance was, partly, also a family. “Make this a regular thing” opens the route to Years Later. “Take it one dinner at a time” changes the terms and carries you toward The Map, Closing.

choices.text: Make this a regular thing
choices.consequence: Build the family slowly. You make this a regular thing. The path to Years Later opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Take it one dinner at a time
choices.consequence: You take it one dinner at a time. The path to The Map, Closing opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Monarch is, in the new public era, oversight more than secrecy. Titans are policy. You have testified before three legislatures. You sleep with the fish your grandfather kept — actually his great-grandfish — on the dresser. Tokyo Apartment, Returned will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Stay in the public role” than after “Hand off and write the family book.”

choices.text: Stay in the public role
choices.consequence: You stay in the public role. The path to Tokyo Apartment, Returned opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Hand off and write the family book
choices.consequence: You choose to hand off and write the family book. By Tokyo Apartment, Returned, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You spend a year visiting every red pin on the original map. Some are empty. Some have new villages. Some have new Titans. You take photographs your grandfather would have wanted. Tokyo Apartment, Returned will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Compile them into an archive” than after “Donate the originals to a museum.”

choices.text: Compile them into an archive
choices.consequence: You commit to compile them into an archive. It carries you toward Tokyo Apartment, Returned, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Donate the originals to a museum
choices.consequence: You commit to donate the originals to a museum. It carries you toward Tokyo Apartment, Returned, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You and Kentaro spend a week in the old Tokyo apartment going through the last drawers. You find the photograph he was holding the day he died — your grandmother, in a doorway, laughing. You decide which life to live next from this room.

choices.text: Stay public; the work calls
choices.consequence: You choose to stay public; the work calls. By Director, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Go home and write the book together
choices.consequence: You choose to go home and write the book together. By The Family Book, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You become a director of public Monarch and, in a strange way, your grandfather's apprentice fifty years late. You preside over a small office full of files that no longer have to be hidden. You like that.

You and Kentaro write a book together about the two lives of your grandfather. It is a strange book — half family memoir, half kaiju field guide. It sells, mysteriously, on every continent. Some readers cry. Some readers leave you weird voicemails. You answer most of them.
